points.quote: The page and its whiteboard are one BlockSuite block tree stored in a single Yjs doc, and "edgeless" is only a different view of it. ... Switching modes changes nothing in the stored data.
The root `affine:page` block has an `affine:surface` child and one or more `affine:note` children. ... They live in the `affine:surface` block's `elements` prop
Canvas-native elements (shape, brush, connector, group, mindmap, text, highlighter) are not blocks. They live in the `affine:surface` block's `elements` prop, a boxed `Y.Map` keyed by element id
The note blocks hold the paragraphs, lists and so on that page mode renders. Page mode shows the notes as a linear document. Edgeless mode shows the same notes as movable cards on the canvas.

Elements that are heavier or document-like are real blocks. These are `affine:note`, `affine:frame`, `affine:image`, ... Apart from notes, they are listed as allowed children of the surface block in its schema metadata.
**Position:** every element and every canvas block has an `xywh` field. It is a serialized string such as `"[x,y,w,h]"`.
**Stacking order:** a fractional-index string in the `index` field (for example `'a0'`) sets the z-order. ... The layer manager sorts blocks and canvas elements together by this index.

A `group` element ... keeps a `children` `Y.Map<boolean>` that maps child id to `true` ... The group's bounds are derived from its children. ... Frames are the other container. They are `affine:frame` blocks that hold child ids in a similar way.
